Hyp page-table mapping creation, protection flags, and translation-control field encodings.
VGIC distributor and redistributor emulation and maintenance-handler behavior.

findings.text: VGIC creation validates the requested model, establishes the VM maximum VCPU count for that model, marks the VM as using an in-kernel controller, finalizes identification registers, provisions per-VCPU private interrupts, and applies model-specific follow-up for newer generations, reporting absence, busy, existence, oversize, or allocation failure as appropriate.

Creation requires the VM lock already held by the caller, then attempts non-blocking acquisition of every online VCPU lock to stabilize VCPU creation and exclude concurrent VCPU ioctls, then holds the architecture configuration mutex while checking and mutating VGIC state, releasing both on all exits.
Creation is rejected when an in-kernel controller already exists, when any VCPU has already run at least once, or when the current online VCPU count exceeds the limit implied by the requested model.

Model handling selects distinct VCPU limits for older generations and a clamped limit for the newest generation, leaves the distributor address undefined, leaves the CPU interface address undefined for the oldest model while initializing the redistributor list for the middle model, enables direct SGI capability where supported, refreshes timer state for the newest model, and on private allocation failure releases partial state and clears model and in-kernel markers.

A small family provides executable private mappings in hyp address space: a public wrapper for executable protection, an internal helper that delegates through a protected hypercall when the host does not own hyp mappings and otherwise aligns the request, reserves a private virtual range, instantiates the mapping, and preserves the original page offset, plus a range allocator that grows downward from a global base.
Private virtual range allocation serializes with a dedicated hyp page-table mutex, and the inner range-commit helper requires that mutex to be held.

Range commitment requires page alignment, rounds sizes up, rejects a request that flips the high address bit relative to the current base as address-space exhaustion, and only updates the observable base and output address on success.
Executable mapping creation is forbidden when the kernel itself runs in hyp mode, and failures leave the caller output cleared rather than partially initialized.

Hyp vector initialization populates a selector table with direct and hardened direct entries derived from kernel hyp addresses, then populates indirect entries from the same base except when idmapped vectors are required outside protected mode, in which case an additional executable mapping supplies the indirect base; a single-slot helper performs each table store.
Hyp per-CPU footprint is the span between dedicated section markers, with a zero order reported for an empty span, and protected SVE host state order is derived from its size helper.

Per-CPU hyp preparation fills a shared parameter block with a tag-cleared per-CPU offset for use through the EL2 thread register, a copy of the memory attribute register, a translated control register honoring HVHE versus classic EL2 layouts plus address-size selection, the hyp page-table base, host hypervisor configuration flags adjusted for protected mode and memory tagging or system-instruction trapping plus HVHE enable, and cleared stage-2 registers, then flushes the block for MMU-off consumption.

Host vector installation first switches to an identity-mapped init vector, asserts finalized capabilities, invokes hyp initialization through a host hypercall passing the parameter block address, and warns when the hypercall does not report success. A companion reset restores stub vectors unless already in hyp mode; non-VHE vulnerable CPUs with the relevant capability request an additional speculation mitigation through hyp, and feature setup selects the vector plus optional timer, debug, and VGIC hardware work.

Per-CPU bring-up is a three-step reinit of reset, context creation, and feature setup, executed once per CPU under an initialized flag, skipped for teardown when protected mode is active, with a virtualization-enable entry that disables preemption before hyp init and raises VGIC and timer subsystems, and a disable entry that lowers timer and VGIC before conditional hyp teardown.

At run time each CPU selects its hyp vector from the precomputed table using its per-CPU hardening slot, writing the hyp-resident vector variable directly in normal mode and delegating the slot update through hyp in protected mode.

Host debug capture records PMU counter count when the performance extension is implemented, breakpoint and watchpoint counts from the debug feature register, and feature flags for profiling, branch records, trace buffering, and preconfigured EL1 tracing, with an early exit on VHE and stricter trace disabling under protected mode.
VHE debug initialization clears stale profiling control enables when the host advertises the profiling extension.

VGIC CPU hardware setup requires a non-preemptible context and clears virtual list registers, using direct control-interface writes for one generation and a hyp call for another generation or compatibility mode; the direct path iterates over the advertised register count writing zeroes through a mapped control base.
CPU online and offline transitions respectively enable and disable the global VGIC maintenance interrupt.

Power-management handling preserves the initialized marker across suspend so resume can distinguish previously enabled CPUs, resets hyp on suspend entry, re-runs full reinit on failed suspend or resume when previously enabled, and ignores other notifications; notifier registration is skipped in protected mode and replaced by empty stubs in an alternate build.
Early setup copies the firmware-to-logical CPU mapping into hyp storage for online CPUs only, and the hyp accessor returns the stored value after validating the index against the table size.

Subsystem initialization enables hyp on every CPU, registers the power notifier, initializes hyp VGIC state and records presence plus CPU-interface and list-register details, tolerates missing VGIC outside protected mode while rejecting nested virtualization without a suitable controller, then initializes hyp timer support, performance callbacks, and hyp tracing where trace failure only logs, unwinding the notifier and hyp enablement on error or whenever protected mode is inactive.

Hyp VGIC probing fails without firmware-provided VGIC info or with a missing maintenance interrupt when masking is available, taints on non-architectural deactivation behavior, dispatches by controller generation with CPU-interface enablement for one generation, records the maintenance interrupt, releases the info block, and requests a per-CPU maintenance handler unless operating maskless without an interrupt.

PSCI relay setup fails protected initialization without a version operation, otherwise captures host PSCI and container versions and, for the oldest specification version, additionally captures function identifiers and per-operation implementation flags.

Hyp trace setup is a no-op when running in hyp mode and in a header-only configuration, refuses when any possible CPU requires a counter workaround that tracing cannot accommodate, otherwise numbers paired hypervisor and host event tables sequentially from zero and registers a remote hypervisor trace region.

The cross-privilege CPU init block logically carries thread-register offset, memory attribute snapshot, translated control value, page-table base address, host hypervisor control flags, and cleared stage-2 table identifiers, sized for cache-line flush before MMU-off use.
Host-to-hyp CPU bring-up uses a dedicated SMCCC hypercall that consumes the physical address of the per-CPU init block and produces a standard success code on completion.
Virtual list registers for one VGIC generation are memory-mapped as 32-bit slots at a fixed four-byte stride from a list-register base offset off the virtual control base.
Out-of-range logical-CPU lookup in hyp and use of VGIC hardware setup in a preemptible context are treated as fatal programming errors rather than recoverable failures.
